_about: Trust decisions taken from AWS, GitHub and GitLab documentation. minioidc mints each token with a key generated at run time, verifies it and evaluates the policy; expect is what the documentation says STS answers.

cases.name: branch policy, push to main
cases.why: sub repo:octo-org/octo-repo:ref:refs/heads/main and aud sts.amazonaws.com are exactly the documented pair

cases.name: branch policy, push to a feature branch
cases.why: StringEquals on sub: refs/heads/feature/login is a different subject

cases.name: branch policy, pull_request run
cases.why: a pull_request run without an environment has sub repo:ORG/REPO:pull_request

cases.name: branch policy, job that names an environment
cases.why: when the job references an environment the sub is repo:ORG/REPO:environment:NAME, even on main

cases.name: branch policy, another repository of the organization
cases.why: the sub names octo-org/sandbox

cases.name: branch policy, token with GitHub's default audience
cases.why: without an audience the token's aud is https://github.com/octo-org, which is not in the provider's ClientIDList

cases.name: environment policy, deploy job in prod
cases.why: the documented environment subject repo:octo-org/octo-repo:environment:prod

cases.name: environment policy, push to main without an environment
cases.why: a role pinned to an environment refuses jobs that do not run in it

cases.name: any-ref policy, pull_request run
cases.why: repo:octo-org/octo-repo:* allows any branch, pull request merge branch or environment

cases.name: any-ref policy, tag push
cases.why: the wildcard covers ref:refs/tags/... as well

cases.name: any-ref policy, another repository
cases.why: the repository part is still fixed

cases.name: any-repo policy, another repository of the organization
cases.why: repo:octo-org/* is any repository or branch within the organization

cases.name: any-repo policy, look-alike organization
cases.why: the slash after the owner name stops octo-org-evil

cases.name: owner-prefix policy, look-alike organization
cases.why: StringLike * matches any characters, so repo:octo-org* also matches repo:octo-org-evil/...

cases.name: aud-only policy, a stranger's repository
cases.why: without a sub condition GitHub Actions from organizations outside your control can assume the role

cases.name: negated sub policy, a stranger's repository
cases.why: StringNotEquals passes for every value it does not list

cases.name: unmapped claim with IfExists, a stranger's repository
cases.why: repository_owner is not a condition key for GitHub, so the key is missing and ...IfExists is true

cases.name: allow any ref, deny pull_request: pull_request run
cases.why: an explicit Deny overrides the Allow

cases.name: allow any ref, deny pull_request: feature push
cases.why: the Deny does not apply, the Allow does

cases.name: immutable subject policy, repository with immutable subjects
cases.why: repo:OWNER@OWNER-ID/REPO@REPO-ID:ref:refs/heads/main

cases.name: immutable subject policy, repository with the previous format
cases.why: the trust policy must match the subject format the repository uses

cases.name: customized subject with job_workflow_ref
cases.why: include_claim_keys repo, context, job_workflow_ref produce the documented subject

cases.name: environment policy, token minted twenty minutes ago
cases.why: GitHub's tokens expire 300 seconds after iat

cases.name: environment policy, provider with two audiences, token for the second
cases.why: the ClientIDList check passes, the :aud condition in the trust policy does not

cases.name: GitLab token, account without a GitLab provider
cases.why: STS looks up the IAM OIDC provider by the token's iss

cases.name: GitLab branch policy, main of the project
cases.why: sub, namespace_id and project_id are condition keys for gitlab.com

cases.name: GitLab branch policy, another project
cases.why: project_id and sub differ
